How each adjustment works

  • Bridge centring (front/back): each hanger hangs from an end beam on a T-plate with 2 bolts in T-nuts. Loosen, slide both hangers to centre the cameras over the part, tighten. ±60 mm.
  • Working distance (both cameras at once): the bridge has an end plate at each end, bolted into the hanger's inner slot (2 bolts each). Loosen, slide the bridge up or down the hangers using the scale, tighten. 300 mm travel: camera bracket 1400 to 1700 above the part, middle 1550.
  • Camera spacing: each camera rides on its own carriage under the bridge (2 bolts, scale on the bridge front face). Set each 350 from the centre mark for 700 axis to axis.
  • Camera vertical: a 3-screw levelling plate between carriage and camera. Level with a small spirit level on the camera body, then confirm with a square target on the bed.
  • Tube lights: 2 cross arms sit on top of the bridge. Each carries 2 light carriages (offset from the camera line, scale on the arm) and a 20 × 20 drop. On each drop a clip block carries a tube-holder bar with 2 tube clips. The clip slides along the drop to set the tube height. The lights move with the cameras.
  • Frame on the bed legs: each post is held to a bed leg by 2 clamp brackets, one just under the bed and one near the lower rail. The posts stop 100 above the floor, so bed, frame, cameras and lights are one unit.
  • Loading: nothing crosses the bed below the top beams, so the part goes in from the front between the two front posts, or from either end.

Cut list (updates with the site dimensions)

To check before detailing
  • 1400 and 1550 together: they leave 150 between the camera bracket face and the lens front for the carriage plate, levelling plate, camera body and lens. Confirm with the chosen camera and lens. If the stack is longer, keep the lens at 1400 with the bridge height adjustment; the bracket then ends up higher than 1550.
  • Bed width and bed height: not given yet. Placeholders 900 and 900; enter the real values above.
  • Ceiling: top beams ≈ 2.6 m above the floor. Check ceiling, overhead lines and crane paths. The existing tube fixture over the bed must come off.
  • Stiffness, rear posts only: the bridge, cameras and lights hang about 0.5 m in front of the two rear posts. Check sway at the cameras with the press cycling. If images blur, use 40 × 80 for the rear posts and end beams, or add gusset plates at the two top corners.
  • Bed carries the frame: check the bed legs and welds. Lock or remove castors if the bed has any.
  • Loading direction: on a 54″ bed the front posts are about 1250 apart (inside faces), so a part longer than that cannot go in from the front. It can slide in from either end, between the end posts. The live checks show both. Confirm the real part size.
  • Bare tubes: use LED tubes with a polycarbonate body (no glass) and holders with a positive lock so a tube cannot drop onto the part. Cover the wiring at the tube end caps. If the bare tubes glare at the operator, a simple top shield can be added later.
  • Light along the part: 1200 tubes over a 1400 part leave the ends dimmer. Check test images, or use 1500 tubes.
  • Lens: not selected yet. The required angle of view is in the checks; use the lens check once the camera is chosen.
  • Safety: end caps on all profile ends, frame earthed. Cables run along the top beams and down a rear post to the control box under the bed.

Assumptions

  • Bed 1372 long (54″) × 140 thick (5.5″) from the sketch; the length runs along the camera line. Bed width 900 and bed top 900 above the floor are placeholders. Legs 50 × 50, 40 in from the bed edges (placeholder).
  • Part envelope 1400 × 800 × 20: placeholder; outline is generic. The part lies along the bed length, so this placeholder overhangs the bed by about 14 at each end.
  • Working distance 1400 = part top surface to lens front. Camera bracket 1550 = part top surface to the camera bracket face (underside of the camera bridge, where the camera carriage bolts on).
  • "Cameras 700 apart" read as 700 between the two camera axes, along the part length, both on the part centre line.
  • Generic camera 45 × 45 × 60 and lens Ø40 × 72 to fit the 150 stack.
  • Required field = part plus 50 mm margin on each edge, at least 50 mm overlap between the two cameras. Pinhole model from the lens front.
  • Lights: 2 bare T8 LED tubes (Ø26) per side, 90 apart, nominal 600 / 1200 / 1500 lengths.
  • Posts stand 35 outside the bed edge so the white sheet and the operator's hands clear them.
  • Profiles: generic 40-series T-slot aluminium; plates in aluminium or mild steel, sized at detailing.
